hypotheses.case_question: What do third-quarter results show against the July guidance for sales and operating income?
hypotheses.what_changed: On July 30 Amazon guided third-quarter net sales of $197.0 billion to $202.0 billion, growth of 9% to 12%. It guided operating income of $22.5 billion to $26.5 billion, against $17.4 billion a year earlier. The company has not revised this guidance since.
hypotheses.positive_case: Results in or above the July ranges would support the case. Second-quarter net sales of $200.6 billion and operating income of $27.5 billion were both above the top of the company's second-quarter ranges. AWS sales grew 37% in that quarter.
hypotheses.counter_case: The guidance names supply volatility for memory chips and energy prices among its risks. Capital spending is rising fast: $96.3 billion of cash capital spending in the first half of 2026, against $55.6 billion a year earlier. Free cash flow over the last twelve months was an outflow of $7.6 billion. The year-earlier operating income of $17.4 billion included a $2.5 billion FTC settlement and $1.8 billion of estimated severance.

evidence_chain.text: The guidance expects an unfavorable currency effect of about 80 basis points (0.8 of a percentage point). No other link from economic data to Amazon was established.
In the second quarter North America sales grew 16%, International 15% and AWS 37%. AWS operating income was $16.6 billion.
The call is at 2:00 p.m. PT on October 29 (21:00 UTC), after that day's close and inside the five-session window. Amazon does not state the results release time.
Second-quarter net income was $62.6 billion, or $5.75 a diluted share, and included $53.4 billion of non-operating other income. The company gives no EPS guidance.

hypotheses.funding_check: The filings reviewed show six note sales in 2026. In March Amazon sold $37.0 billion of U.S. dollar notes and €14.5 billion of euro notes. It sold CHF2.8 billion of Swiss franc notes in May and C$14.0 billion of Canadian dollar notes in June. In July it sold $25.0 billion of U.S. dollar notes. A sale of £4.25 billion of sterling notes closed September 14. In June Amazon also entered into a $17.5 billion delayed-draw term loan (a loan from a group of lenders that it could take in one draw). It could draw it on or before September 30, 2026. Any amount not drawn by then ended. Nothing was borrowed under it at June 30. The filings reviewed do not say whether Amazon drew it. Amazon expects more financing in 2026. It invested $15.0 billion in OpenAI in the first quarter, $13.7 billion in the second and $21.3 billion after June 30. Equity stakes in private companies, mainly Anthropic and OpenAI, were carried at $122.3 billion at June 30.
